title: Uniform law of the conditioned disjoint-coordinate vector
statement: Let $n \ge 1$ and fix a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Consider the hard distribution on samples, conditioned both on the event that the generated pair of sets is disjoint and on the special coordinate being equal to $i$. Then the generated vector of disjoint coordinates, viewed as a map $\{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\text{neither}, \text{leftOnly}, \text{rightOnly}\}$, has the same law as the identity map applied to a vector drawn uniformly at random from all such maps; that is, under this conditioning the generated vector is uniformly distributed over the $3^n$ possible coordinate assignments.
